text: The issue is simple and can be addressed automatically.
A how-to or FAQ: password reset, Bluetooth pairing, order tracking, firmware, or account settings.
The customer wants instructions. Nothing is broken, missing, disputed, or unsafe.
A routine question. Not a fault, refund, replacement, or complaint.
A published help article answers it. No investigation and no decision.
How to use the product, the app, or the website.
They ask how to do something and do not report a failure or a charge.
Standard self-service steps will resolve it without a person.
Setup, login, finding an order, or a question about published store policy.
Instructions only. No refund, replacement, cancellation, or security incident.
The hardware issue or replacement request needs a human agent.
A defect, replacement, refund, billing dispute, or damaged delivery.
Something failed, money is at stake, or a human must judge the case.
Broken hardware, a refund, a safety issue, or an account takeover.
A specialist must investigate, decide, or make an exception.
Warranty, return, cancellation, wrong item, or a complaint to resolve.
A physical product problem, a charge error, or an action only staff can take.
Faults, refunds, replacements, missing orders, security, legal, or safety.
A real order or device problem that support staff must handle.
The customer is blocked, out of pocket, or at risk, and a person should take over.
The message is spam or completely irrelevant.
Spam, phishing, or a scam, including a fake delivery or account alert.
An unsolicited sales pitch, supplier offer, or partnership request.
Recruitment, a job application, or a message meant for someone else.
Gibberish or an automated notice with no question for support.
Marketing, crypto, selling followers, or a prize promotion.
The sender does not describe a problem with their own order, account, or device.
Cold outreach. Nobody is asking us to fix, explain, or replace something.
Phishing that asks for a password, a payment, or card details.
Not a customer support request.
